title: A wet dog at the door
text: A dog comes home after a [[muddy|MUD]] walk in the rain. It shakes, and water goes everywhere. Then its owner [[carefully|CARE]] puts a towel over it. The dog is dry in the next shot. The advert [[clearly|CLEAR]] shows when the towel is [[useful|USE]]. Dog owners may think of their own wet floors at home.
source: Master Lists/advert analysis paragraphs.csv line 81 (edited: added muddy, carefully, clearly)

title: The picture at the end of the lesson
text: A child starts a [[drawing|DRAW]] with a small blue circle. At the end of the art lesson, the circle is the centre of a big, [[colourful/colorful|COLOUR]] flower. The advert shows the start and the finished picture. A [[beginner|BEGIN]] can see that a picture can grow from one [[simple|SIMPLY]] shape on the page.
source: Master Lists/advert analysis paragraphs.csv line 149 (edited: added colourful)

title: A cup left on the train
text: The advert begins with a cup left on a train seat. A [[cleaner|CLEAN]] finds it and puts it in a box at the station. Its [[owner|OWN]] comes back and takes it home. The story shows how the lost property [[service|SERVE]] works. [[Travellers/Travelers|TRAVEL]] may feel better knowing where to ask if they forget something.

title: The price written on the mirror
text: In a hairdresser’s advert, the price of a haircut appears on the mirror beside the customer. [[Viewers|VIEW]] see it while watching the barber work. Putting the price in the scene makes it [[easy|EASE]] to notice. Someone who is [[worried|WORRY]] about the cost can [[decide|DECISION]] if the haircut is within their budget.
source: Master Lists/advert analysis paragraphs.csv line 268 (edited: ‘who worries’ became ‘who is worried’)

title: The sticker on a fruit box
text: A large ‘Wonky but tasty’ sticker [[appears|APPEARANCE]] on a box of oddly shaped apples. One apple is much wider on one side, but a photograph on the label shows it cut open with clean white flesh inside. The words make the [[unusual|USUAL]] shape sound playful, and the photo addresses a more [[practical|PRACTICE]] concern. [[Shoppers|SHOP]] can see why the apples might still be worth buying.

title: A tyre on a wet corner
text: The tyre advert shows the same car turning a corner twice on a wet road. A line marks where each turn begins. The [[comparison|COMPARE]] helps viewers see how the tyres affect the car’s path. [[Drivers|DRIVE]] who worry about rain may pay more [[attention|ATTEND]] to that visible [[difference|DIFFERENT]] than to a list of facts.

title: One wheel on the white line
text: In a tyre advert, the camera follows one wheel as it passes from dry road to standing water. There is no cut at the point where the road surface changes. That continuous shot makes the [[demonstration|DEMONSTRATE]] easier to follow because [[viewers|VIEW]] can watch the same wheel through both conditions. For [[cautious|CAUTION]] drivers, the [[visible|VISIBILITY]] change in the road may carry more [[weight|WEIGH]] than a general promise of good grip.

title: The electric car without an engine note
text: At a red light, the driver lowers her window and hears a [[conversation|CONVERSE]] on the pavement. The advert leaves the voices in the mix as the car pulls away. By letting an ordinary sound remain audible, it gives viewers a way to [[judge|JUDGEMENT]] how quietly the car moves. For [[buyers|BUY]] who associate a [[strong|STRENGTH]] engine with a loud one, the scene also [[invites|INVITATION]] them to see quietness as a sign of progress.

title: A shoe advert without a finish line
text: Rather than follow the runner to a [[triumphant|TRIUMPH]] ending, the camera cuts away while she is still climbing a hill. The shoes remain visible, but the outcome is [[unresolved|RESOLVE]]. This refusal to promise victory gives the advert a quieter [[argument|ARGUE]]. For viewers who run without competing, [[persistence|PERSIST]] may be more [[recognisable/recognizable|RECOGNISE]] than the usual celebration at the finish.

title: A building shown while being built
text: The housing advert includes [[unfinished|FINISH]] stairs, exposed walls and workers still on site. It asks buyers to [[imagine|IMAGINATION]] the future apartments from a space that is visibly incomplete. This may make the process feel transparent, but plans can change between [[construction|CONSTRUCT]] and completion. Prospective [[residents|RESIDE]] need the final specifications as well as a [[persuasive|PERSUADE]] vision.
